business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Density Hyperscale Server Facility Mechanical and Cooling EPC

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Unitary National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified, with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation per Article 2 of the Egyptian Constitution)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1982, entered into force 1992)
Egypt-UK Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1975)
US-Egypt Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 1980, effective 1982)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Law No. 80 of 2016 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended (including Law No. 154 of 2019), its Executive Regulations, Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT regulations, and instructions issued by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU). UBO register: Law No. 180 of 2018 promulgating the Companies Law, as amended by Law No. 149 of 2019, and its Executive Regulations enforced by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), which mandate the disclosure and maintenance of registered beneficial ownership data at incorporation; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Existence of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registrar (e.g., UK Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate in the jurisdiction of issuance (Hague Apostille inapplicable - Egypt is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized board resolution (extract of minutes) of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing the incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing its authorized signatories and local representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary and home-country notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian consular post in the country of execution; apostille not recognized by Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney granted by each foreign shareholder and UBO to the local incorporation agent or law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public (or Egyptian notary public if executed in Egypt)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization where executed abroad; Egyptian domestic notarization where executed in Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport and identity copies, and police clearance certificates, of all directors and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country passport authority and police authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate; apostille not accepted

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association of the Egyptian LLC (founders' signatures authenticated before the GAFI-accredited notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Egyptian notarization only (no consular or apostille step for domestic execution)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Law No. 80 of 2016 and Central Bank of Egypt regulations: screen all directors, UBOs, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK sanctions lists where applicable, the EMLCU national terrorist designation lists, and domestic suspicious-transaction indicators. PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence requiring source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior management approval, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. For this ISIC 4100 data-center EPC scope, classified as Low_Risk_Standard, standard customer due diligence applies subject to a 25% UBO look-through at incorporation and continuous screening of public-sector procurement counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop Electronic Incorporation Portal and Commercial Registry Information System (gafi.gov.eg), operated jointly by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones and the Commercial Registry offices under Law No. 34 of 1976
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Arabic is the mandatory script for the statutory company name. A Latin (English) transliteration may be registered as a secondary trade name provided it is a faithful phonetic transliteration of the Arabic name. The LLC suffix must appear as the Arabic abbreviation 'ذ.م.م' or the Latin abbreviation 'LLC' at the end of the name in all corporate filings, and must be consistent across the Arabic and transliterated versions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Insurance, Securities, Investment Fund, Clearing, Finance (reserved; require prior Central Bank of Egypt or Financial Regulatory Authority licensing)
Egypt, Arab Republic of Egypt, President, Ministry, Minister, Government, Public Authority, Municipality (require prior ministerial approval)
National, Military, Army, Police, Security, Force (public-order and sovereign-attribute objections)
Islamic, Christian, Mosque, Church and other religious or sectarian references (require prior authorization and raise public-order sensitivity)
United Nations, International Monetary Fund, World Bank and other international-organization or foreign-state identifiers (prohibited without official consent)
Identical or confusingly similar duplicate of an already-registered trade name in the Commercial Registry (refusal per Law No. 34 of 1976)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, GAFI issues a written refusal stating the legal basis. The applicant may: (1) submit a redress request to the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching evidence of prior use, distinctiveness, or registered trademark rights; (2) in trademark-collision cases, obtain a written coexistence or assignment from the prior rights holder and resubmit the application; (3) appeal the final administrative refusal before the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 60 days of the final decision. Pending an appeal, a modified provisional alternative name may be reserved to avoid delaying incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as the sole registered office for an ISIC 4100 construction and EPC entity. GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Tax Authority require a verifiable physical address in Egypt supported by a notarized lease or title deed. Virtual-office mail-forwarding services may supplement, but cannot replace, the statutory Egyptian registered office disclosed in the memorandum of association.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High: estimated 45% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months, driven by GAFI commercial-substance audits, VAT-registration premises verification, labor and social-insurance field inspections, and project-site supervision typical of EPC operations. Mitigation requires continuous staffed presence at the registered office during business hours and retention of original lease and utility documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and preliminary reservation fee through the GAFI Commercial Registry database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GAFI statutory tariff schedule for name search and reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LLC incorporation filing, Commercial Registry registration, and issuance of the electronic incorporation certificate (GAFI one-stop-shop, including notarization of the memorandum of association)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under Law No. 180 of 2018 and Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization and notarization bundle for foreign corporate documentation (certificate of good standing, board resolution, powers of attorney, identity documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Department, Egyptian embassies/consulates abroad, and home-country notaries
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff schedule and prevailing notarial market benchmark (approximately USD 60-120 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the memorandum of association and incorporation notice in the Egyptian Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriyya)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff per page under the Official Gazette regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial beneficial ownership (UBO) disclosure filing and GAFI register annotation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GAFI e-services administrative fee for UBO register updates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year physical registered office lease agreement (approximately 50 sqm Grade-B administrative office in Cairo, including notarization and lease registration with GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private landlord and Egyptian notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Cairo Grade-B commercial lease market benchmark and Egyptian notarial tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation and notary attestation of all foreign-issued documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed translation office and Egyptian notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Egyptian Notarial Tariff Law and translation-industry association benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Local counsel flat legal fee for pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance handling, AML/UBO piercing and beneficial-ownership analysis, and LLC incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark flat fee for standard LLC incorporation in the infrastructure EPC sector

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 148 of 2019), Articles 20-33 (LLC formation, quota subscription, management); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations for GAFI one-stop-shop procedures; Commercial Code No. 17/1999 for registration provisions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop (OLP), Cairo Headquarters and affiliated governorate offices.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association (Aqd Ta'sis / عقد تأسيس الشركة ذات المسؤولية المحدودة) executed in Arabic before a licensed Egyptian Notary Public and submitted via GAFI e-registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No numeric statutory minimum capital for LLCs under Law 159/1981; capital must be adequate for the corporate purpose, fully divided into quotas and fully subscribed by all founding partners. Cash consideration must be deposited in an escrow account opened with a licensed Egyptian commercial bank in the company's formation name, with the deposit certificate lodged at GAFI. In-kind contributions must be supported by an independent valuation report. Escrowed funds are released only upon issuance of the GAFI incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LLC

Adopted by the founding partners on [DATE] under Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 148 of 2019):
1. The Notary-verified Memorandum of Association is ratified.
2. One hundred percent of the share capital quotas are subscribed as provided in Schedule A.
3. The paid-up cash portion shall be held in escrow at [Bank], Cairo, until GAFI issues the incorporation certificate.
4. The registered office is fixed at [Address], Cairo Governorate.
5. [NAME] is appointed Manager with sole legal representation authority.
6. [NAME] is appointed Company Secretary and [FIRM] statutory auditor.

The Manager is authorized to complete all corporate registrations and licensing. Unanimously resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop online name reservation module (https://www.gafi.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed Arabic trade names together with an English transliteration through the GAFI online commercial name reservation system. Confirm that no existing entity bears an identical or confusingly similar name. Obtain the electronic name approval certificate, which remains valid for 60 calendar days and is required for subsequent notarization steps.
required_dossiers: Primary proposed name and two alternatives
Certified passport or national ID copies of all founding partners
Notarized power of attorney if a local formation agent is instructed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused, submit an administrative appeal to the GAFI Name Committee with a modified distinctive element and pay the EGP 200 re-processing fee; alternatively select a new proposed name and restart the reservation workflow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Legal Review, and Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Legal Vetting Unit and the Egyptian Notary Public Office (Ma'mouria) serving the company's registered office district
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an Egyptian licensed corporate lawyer to draft the Arabic Memorandum of Association, covering the corporate name, object (design, procurement, installation, commissioning and maintenance of electromechanical systems for hyperscale data centers), capital structure, management rules and dispute resolution. Obtain GAFI preliminary legal vetting, then arrange execution of the document by all founders or their authorized attorneys before the public notary, with notarial certification of signatures and any corrections.
required_dossiers: Arabic draft Memorandum of Association in triplicate
GAFI corporate name approval certificate
Valid national ID or passport of each founding partner
Bank escrow confirmation letter (preliminary) if capital deposit precedes notarization
Certified Arabic translation of any foreign corporate shareholder's charter and board authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or GAFI queries completeness, cure by delivering resubmitted corrected signature pages or revised articles, and obtain Egyptian consular attestation of foreign execution deeds within 30 days; no new name approval is required if the legal name remains unchanged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit into Temporary Escrow Account and Bank Issuance of Formation Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g. National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, Commercial International Bank) with GAFI-compliant escrow desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company under formation, deposit the agreed paid-up cash capital from each founding partner, and instruct the bank to issue an official Arabic deposit certificate addressed to GAFI confirming the balances and the legal holder. The bank is contractually barred from releasing funds until presentation of the final GAFI incorporation certificate. Any in-kind contribution must be covered by a valuation report attached to the certificate.
required_dossiers: GAFI name approval certificate
Notarized Memorandum of Association (draft or final)
Valid identification documents of all signatories to the escrow account
Source of funds declaration for each contributing partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank triggers enhanced due diligence, provide proof of residential address, corporate ownership charts for foreign entities, and a Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) inbound remittance advice confirming the lawful origin of funds; upon refusal, transfer the escrow to an alternative approved bank and re-issue the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Final Incorporation Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Formation with Commercial Register Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department – One-Stop Shop (OLP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File at the GAFI One-Stop Shop the notarized Memorandum of Association, the bank escrow certificate, and the statutory forms; pay the prescribed registration and publication fees (approximately EGP 15,000-20,000); obtain, on a single integrated workflow, the GAFI Incorporation Certificate, the Commercial Registry (Al-Sijil Al-Tijari) extract, the tax card registration number, and the preliminary social insurance number. The company is legally constituted upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
Bank escrow deposit certificate
GAFI name approval certificate
Minutes of the founding partners approving the memorandum
Appointment letter and specimen signature of the Manager
GAFI fee payment voucher
Lease contract or title deed for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query or deficiency notice, respond in writing within 15 business days through the appointed Manager or legal counsel, submit any corrected notarized instruments, and retain the same filing queue without additional registration fees; unresolved queries may be escalated to the GAFI Internal Appeals Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, VAT, Payroll, and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Tax and VAT Departments; Social Insurance Authority; licensed commercial bank for the permanent account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Utilize the tax and social insurance numbers automatically generated by the GAFI One-Stop Shop to finalize registration under the Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 and VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 at the competent ETA office. Apply for the corporate tax card and VAT certificate, then open the permanent corporate bank account, activate official accounting books, and register employees and engineers for social insurance and payroll withholding. File the statutory auditor appointment notice with the ETA.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial Registry extract
Form 1/110 and tax card applications
VAT registration application
Lease contract of the registered office
Auditor appointment letter
Bank account opening package and signature cards
National ID copies of all employees and payroll schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA lodges a late registration or compliance penalty, file a voluntary disclosure with mitigating circumstances, request administrative waiver or penalty reduction under the tax amnesty provisions, and implement accounting software within 30 days to demonstrate prospective compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Gazette Publication, Chamber of Commerce Admission, and EFCBC Electromechanical Contracting Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Misriya) at the Ministry of Justice; Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce; Egyptian Federation for Construction and Building Contractors (EFCBC) Classification Committee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory incorporation extract in the Commercial Gazette within 60 days of registration; enrol the LLC with the competent Chamber of Commerce; obtain the EFCBC contracting classification certificate for electromechanical works (Class A or B depending on turnover and technical capability) to lawfully bid and execute data center EPC contracts. Additionally register the supervising engineers and project managers with the Engineering Syndicate under the Engineers Law No. 66 of 1974.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial Registry extract
Company letterhead and official contacts form
Memorandum of Association covering data center EPC activity
Chief engineer employment contracts and engineering syndicate cards
Health, safety, and environment manual for construction works
Financial statements or bank experience certificate supporting EFCBC classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late Gazette publication is curable by paying the prescribed late fee and obtaining the Ministry of Justice publication permit; an EFCBC classification refusal may be cured by engaging a technical partner with a superior classification, completing the Egyptian engineering capacity audit, and resubmitting; appeal any adverse decision within 30 days to the EFCBC Higher Classification Board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Organization for Industrial Development (GOFI / IDA) under the Ministry of Trade and Industry, acting jointly with the Egyptian Federation for Construction and Building Contractors (EFCBC) for electromechanical contracting classification and site execution permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Contracting and Electromechanical Works License and EFCBC Classification Certificate (Class A/B for Mechanical and Electrical Data Center EPC) together with the site-specific Industrial Facility/Operating License under the Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment, Environmental Licensing Department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental screening and Preliminary Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) approval required for data center mechanical/electromechanical installation projects; a Full EIA Report is mandated only where the project incorporates a stand-alone central cooling plant or cogeneration (CCHP) capacity above 5 MW.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer must not exceed BOD 60 mg/L, COD 80 mg/L, and TSS 60 mg/L (Law No. 93 of 1962 and Decree 44/2000); use of ozone-depleting refrigerants prohibited under Law No. 4 of 1994 and Ministerial Decree 339/2021; site dust emissions limited to 50 mg/Nm3; boundary noise level capped at 65 dB(A) during daytime operations; diesel backup generators restricted to 24-hour operation per incident with compliance to Decree 372/1994 air emission thresholds; hazardous wastes (coolants, spent batteries, oily rags) must be transported by licensed carriers under the EEAA manifest system to approved disposal sites, with refrigerant leak events reported to EEAA within 24 hours.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Pre-occupancy Civil Defense Certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) verifying fire-fighting equipment, emergency egress, alarm systems, and compliance with the Egyptian Fire Protection Code; structural load and seismic soundness certificate issued by a licensed engineering firm for cooling towers, CRAC units, and roof-mounted plant; Ministry of Manpower occupational health and safety clearance covering HV/electrical work permits, confined-space protocols, compressor maintenance, and respiratory protection; periodic inspection of scaffolds, lifts, hazardous energy lockout/tagout, and emergency response drills before commencement of routine operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - AKA Al-Maslahah Al-Daribiyah Al-Misriyah (الهيئة المصرية العامة للضرائب); official portal www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing/e-receipts platform www.einvoice-tax.gov.eg; customs single-window NAFIZA (www.nafiza.gov.eg). Large-scale EPC contractors are generally administered by the ETA Large Taxpayer Center (Cairo).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned EG LLC must obtain (1) a unified 9-digit Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) reflected on the 'Tax Card' (Kard Daribia) and (2) a separate VAT registration number. Procedure: (a) incorporate the LLC at the Commercial Registry via GAFI one-stop-shop and complete social insurance registration; (b) apply for the Tax Card at the competent ETA tax office attaching the certificate of incorporation, notarized by-laws and board resolutions, power of attorney of the local general manager, Egyptian premises lease/title, passports of directors/shareholders, and the company ledger; the statutory application window is up to 30 days; (c) upon annual taxable supplies exceeding EGP 500,000 (or voluntarily at formation, or immediately upon a taxable import), submit the VAT registration application to the ETA VAT desk within 30 days of the threshold; (d) activate the ETA e-invoice 'taxpayer wallet' and obtain the qualified e-invoice certificate/signature. A non-resident entity without a fixed establishment cannot hold an Egyptian VAT registration in its own name; the EG LLC is the local tax registrant for the EPC project.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the EG LLC is a fully taxable juridical person with no fiscal transparency and no pass-through eligibility; resident Egyptian companies are taxed on worldwide income (Law 91/2005 Art. 2) at the standard 22.5% CIT rate. A foreign parent maintaining only a branch/PE in Egypt is taxed on Egyptian-source income, with a deemed-profit regime of 15% of annual contract receipts for foreign contractors. The entity does not benefit from the Tax_Exempt_Zone default; Free Zone / Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) exemptions under Law 83/2002 and Law 7/2015 are elective locational privileges, not ordinary LLC classifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box and no entity-classification election exists under Egyptian law; hybrid mismatch recharacterization of the LLC is rejected absent an express treaty provision. Statutory elections available in computing tax liability include: (i) depreciation method election (straight-line at ministerial rates or declining balance) per asset pool; (ii) fiscal year election only with Minister of Finance approval (statutory year is the calendar year); (iii) application of the 85% participation exemption for dividends/capital gains from qualifying shareholdings of at least 25% held for at least 2 years versus full inclusion; (iv) ordinary foreign tax credit (per-country credit limit) instead of deduction; (v) loss carryforward of up to 5 years (no carryback) subject to ownership continuity; and (vi) treaty relief via Egypt double-tax agreements. There is no group/consolidated filing election for related Egyptian LLCs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Egyptian VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended, implemented by ETA decrees including MoF Decision No. 420/2020 (e-invoicing), Decision No. 370/2022 (e-receipts), and the NAFIZA customs integration rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods/services under Article 15 of Law 67/2016; registration is mandatory within 30 days of the threshold being exceeded. Importation of goods into Egypt for use in a taxable economic activity also triggers VAT registration irrespective of the threshold. EPC contractors performing taxable construction supplies in Egypt are registrants even if the principal is non-resident.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance for all VAT-registered entities through the ETA e-invoicing platform (national rollout phased from 15 November 2020 to 31 May 2023). The supplier submits each tax invoice in XML/JSON via REST/SOAP API or the web portal; the ETA validates against the registered counterparty master data, tariff/tax codes, and supply logic in near-real time, then returns a validation decision. Only cleared invoices bear the mandatory QR stamp/unique validation UUID and are legally recognized for input VAT deduction and customs clearance; buyers must perform electronic confirmation. E-receipts (POS digital receipts) are additionally mandatory for B2C transactions from January 2023. Non-compliance penalty is EGP 50,000 per violation under Decision 420/2020; the ETA may suspend the taxpayer's e-invoice wallet and disallow input credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 6(1) of Law 67/2016, exported goods are zero-rated when they physically leave Egypt under a customs export declaration. Under Article 6(2), services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident party and used, exploited, and consumed entirely outside Egypt; this covers offshore design/engineering and foreign procurement components of a datacenter EPC. Services connected to Egyptian real estate - on-site civil, electro-mechanical, and cooling system installation - are treated as Egyptian-location supplies taxable at 14% even when the principal is foreign; zero-rating is restricted to the offshore-scope deliverables. Additional ETA conditions for 0% VAT: registered exporter status, receipt of the consideration in convertible foreign currency, repatriation of proceeds to Egypt through the banking system, issuance of an ETA-validated export e-invoice with the zero-rated code, and timely filing of the VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NAFIZA customs export declaration (Cargo Export Declaration) reflecting the zero-rated export entry and confirming the exporter TIN
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of goods from Egyptian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by the Egyptian bank proving receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds
Foreign currency export proceeds statement/contract (CBE export proceeds form) with the bank's repatriation stamp
ETA-approved zero-rated export e-invoice carrying the validation UUID and QR stamp
EPC contract, purchase orders, work completion and acceptance certificates, and, for exported services, the foreign client's certificate of offshore use/consumption
Supporting input-VAT documentation (purchase ledger, supplier e-invoices, and customs import receipts) tracing inputs to the exported scope
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may audit export zero-rating within the general 5-year assessment window (extended to 6 years in cases of fraud). Failure to substantiate export status or discovery of fictitious/circular exports results in: (i) retrospective reversal of the 0% rate to 14% VAT on the full export value, with clawback of all input VAT credits claimed and assessed interest at the Central Bank of Egypt credit rate plus 2% per month; (ii) under Article 46 of VAT Law 67/2016, intentional evasion carries imprisonment of 5 to 7 years and a fine of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 in addition to full tax repayment; (iii) false customs declarations attract smuggling penalties under Customs Law 207/2020, including forfeiture and fines of not less than the evaded duties; and (iv) non-repatriation of export proceeds beyond 180 days violates Foreign Exchange Law 194/2020 and the CBE export-proceeds regulations, exposing the exporter to monetary sanctions, disqualification from export incentives, and potential criminal liability for exchange-law violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under the Central Bank and Banking Sector Law No. 194 of 2020, together with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) for capital registration and the Foreign Trade Facilitation Authority for export/import trade documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction and maintains current-account convertibility for bona fide trade, services, dividends, and branch remittances once supported by underlying documentation and tax clearance. Capital-account transactions, including shareholder loans, liquidation proceeds, portfolio transfers, and repatriation of invested capital, remain subject to documentary review, CBE classification, GAFI registration, and sourcing checks. Profit remittance is generally lawful, but banks must verify audited financial statements, corporate tax receipts, beneficial ownership, and the absence of pending AML findings. There is no statutory guarantee of free convertibility for speculative or unregistered capital flows; resident and non-resident entities must settle through CBE-licensed banks and licensed exchange houses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE rules, export proceeds must be repatriated through an Egyptian authorized bank and credited to a foreign-currency or EGP account within the statutory period reflected in CBE instructions, generally not exceeding 180 days from the date of shipment or completion of the EPC installation certificate, unless an approved extension is obtained. The mandatory conversion ratio is applied at the CBE market rate and is currently 100% for general export receivables, unless the CBE grants a case-by-case exemption permitting the retention of foreign currency for documented import or debt-service obligations. For datacenter electromechanical EPC services, the engineer's progress certificate, customs export declaration, and the underlying contract must be lodged with the receiving bank so that the proceeds are tracked against the original invoiced amount.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Moderate for core treasury operations. Offshore fintech and electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not recognized by the CBE as authorized banks for EGP clearing, RTGS participation, or capital-account FX conversion. Such EMIs may be used only as auxiliary collection tools for smaller trade advances or cross-border overhead payments, provided the substantive settlement, tax remittance, payroll, and profit repatriation are completed through a CBE-licensed tier-1 bank. Legal constraints include the prohibition on maintaining EGP nostro accounts offshore, CBE approval for any foreign-currency account, and heightened AML/CFT scrutiny over funds routed through non-bank payment providers.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for non-resident directors, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners during initial onboarding at a CBE-licensed bank. A face-to-face KYC interview at the Egyptian branch is standard practice, especially for an EPC company receiving foreign capital injections and making cross-border disbursements. Remote onboarding is available only for local directors who have already completed physical KYC at the bank and hold valid Egyptian identification; foreign UBOs will normally require a bank-origin notarized power of attorney and a notarized copy of a passport, but most banks still require the foreign principal to attend an interview or to be contacted by a compliance officer through a verified video call. Practical planning should assume a 2 to 4 week onboarding timeline with at least one on-site visit by the Egyptian local manager or authorized director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with ultimate beneficial owners residing in OFAC, EU, UN, or UK-sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full corporate ownership chain from the Egyptian LLC up to the ultimate natural person; third-party sanctions screening report; passport copies; residency proof; signed beneficial ownership declaration; group-level compliance certification; and legal opinion confirming that no OFAC/EU/UN sanctions apply to the contracting parties or end clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque source of funds for the initial share capital injection, particularly when the investment exceeds the shareholder's known operating cash flow.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit audited group financial statements for the last three years; board resolution approving the capital transfer; bank reference letter from the remitting bank; source-of-wealth statement with supporting asset or retained-earnings documentation; and a CBE/GAFI capital registration request referencing the project EPC contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: State-linked or public-sector client creates a PEP or corruption-sensitive red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain the contracting entity's commercial register and board appointment resolutions; include the official tender award document; signed PEP declaration for all directors and UBOs; beneficial ownership registers; independent verification of the parent/state relationship; and a compliance-approved counterparty due-diligence file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial documents, LC, and invoice values do not perfectly match the underlying EPC schedule, triggering trade-based money laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain the fully signed EPC contract, alphabetized variation orders, installment schedule, progress certificates signed by the engineer, original customs declarations, proforma invoices, final invoices, and transportation or bill-of-lading records; reconcile every disbursement to a specific stage of the contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of high-risk intermediary subcontractors or tax-haven invoicing for electromechanical equipment procurement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide subcontractor KYC packs; commercial-register copies; tax identification certificates; proof of physical office and operational capability; invoices and warehouse or customs clearance evidence; independent equipment valuation or expert certificate; and a group AML/CFT policy covering third-party procurement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound direct investment funds from the foreign parent must be wired to the Egyptian LLC's foreign-currency capital account at a CBE-licensed bank using SWIFT MT103, with the remittance instruction clearly coded as 'Direct Investment – Share Subscription / Capital Contribution' under the CBE's designated purpose-code framework. The receiving bank will prepare the inward remittance certificate and GAFI investment registration file; the funds may then be converted into EGP through the interbank market at the prevailing CBE rate. The transaction must be supported by the LLC's certificate of incorporation, board/shareholder resolution authorizing the increase or payment of capital, a statement of the EPC project purpose, and the foreign parent's audited financial statements. Banks must verify that the funds do not represent third-party financing disguised as equity and that no portion is attributable to unnamed beneficial owners.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for imported cooling systems, electrical equipment, and cross-border subcontractor services must be made through CBE-licensed banks using SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments, MT202 for bank-to-bank settlement, or commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) opened under an LC facility. LC issuance requires the underlying import contract, proforma invoice, payment terms, and, where applicable, prior CBE or trade authority approval. Large EGP disbursements to local subcontractors are routed through the CBE RTGS/EGP clearing system; USD liquidity for import LCs is allocated by the bank according to CBE priorities, and disbursements must be supported by customs releases or verified shipping documents. The treasury structure must maintain separate accounts for operational EGP expense, foreign-currency import LC collateral, and government-mandated tax/social insurance suspense to avoid commingling.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable EGP/USD forward contracts with a CBE-licensed bank for maturities not exceeding 12 months, used solely to hedge contracted EPC receivables or known capital-import obligations.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for project debt or equipment-lease liabilities, executed through an Egyptian authorized bank and recorded in the bank's risk-management system.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only when the underlying exposure cannot be fully covered onshore, subject to a documented non-speculative hedging rationale and compliance sign-off.
Simple spot FX trades for immediate conversion of foreign-currency receipts into EGP or settlement currency for payroll, materials, and taxes.
Currency options or structured forwards requiring prior CBE approval and limited strictly to hedge of real contracted cash flows, with no leveraged or speculative overlay.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year-end; calendar-year companies must file on or before 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties range from EGP 1,000 to EGP 5,000; repeated non-compliance triggers a GAFI show-cause notice and administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April following the end of the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a monthly penalty of EGP 500 with interest on unpaid tax; prolonged default leads to enforced collection measures, attachment of bank accounts, and suspension of tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Commercial Registry / GAFI investor services portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first calendar month after the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed renewal attracts a fine of EGP 300 per month; failure to renew for more than 90 days results in removal from the commercial register and administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation and entity data update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI and the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) via the one-stop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation required by 31 March; any shareholding or UBO change must be reported within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance under Egyptian AML Law 80/2002 triggers civil fines of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000; continued failure may suspend licences, restrict banking operations, and lead to judicial strike-off orders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all Egyptian LLCs irrespective of size, turnover, or asset thresholds; no exemptions under the Egyptian Companies Law 159/1981, as replaced by Law 127/2018, or under the Investment Law 72/2017.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS; companies operating under GAFI investment guarantees must apply EAS for all statutory reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each LLC must maintain a current register of beneficial owners and file an annual confirmation with GAFI and the FIU. Any transfer or change in shareholding, directorship, or ultimate beneficial owner must be updated in the statutory registers and reported within 15 days; the annual confirmation, including the UBO register and entity economic-substance declaration, must be submitted by 31 March each year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory headline rate for Egyptian resident LLCs is 22.5%. No blanket tax holiday applies to a mainland EPC LLC; however, an LLC licensed as a free-zone entity (public free zone or Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone)) may benefit from a 0% corporate income tax rate for up to 15 years if approved. Onshore Investment Law No. 72/2017 allows a tax deduction of 30%–50% of eligible investment cost for certain strategic industries and regions, including high-tech infrastructure projects. Mandatory loss carryforward of 5 years and non-deductibility of certain expenses reduce the effective rate to the statutory level or below during early project years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return Form No. 100 (Form 100) submitted electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (taxa.gov.eg / ETA electronic services).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional corporate income tax declarations (Form 100-A) and claim-for-advance-payment settlements are required during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form 100 must be filed, and the final corporate income tax liability settled, no later than four months after the end of the taxable fiscal year. For a calendar-year LLC, the due date is 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, commercial registration number, tax card number, immovable/land registry number, tax year covered, and ETA payer number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Be identical to the Egyptian commercial register and foreign capital investment certificate; state the Egyptian address of the registered branch. For a non-resident parent or investor, the local branch's Form 100 must reference the parent tax identification and treaty residency.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit or loss before taxation per independently audited IFRS/EGAAP financial statements attached to the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert all foreign currency revenue/expenses into EGP using the central bank rate at each transaction date; include all revenues earned from Egyptian sources, including EPC contract milestone payments and change orders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses (excessive entertainment, CSR unregistered, donations without license, local and foreign taxes paid except WHT, asset impairments not recognized by tax law) and deduct tax-exempt income (reversal of provisions, capital gains exemptions, DTA relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not deduct head-office general and administrative charges without a valid cost-sharing agreement and intra-Egypt supporting invoices; apply arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments; attach schedule TP-A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose every controlled transaction with related enterprises, including management fees, sub-contracting, software licensing, equipment purchase, and financing; in precise EGP and currency of transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident contractors and affiliates must include contracts, valuations, and the transfer pricing benchmarking report referenced by master/local file schedules. For non-resident intermediate holding companies, the disclosure also activates the Egyptian ultimate-parent CBCR and master file filing obligation where group turnover exceeds the threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of final withholding taxes previously withheld on interest, royalties, and technical/management fees received by the LLC from Egyptian debtors, reduced by the statutory corporate income tax to a final advance credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Withholding Tax Certificate (Form 11) from each Egyptian payer. Non-resident lenders receiving interest shall obtain ETA-approved DTA relief certificates enabling a reduced withholding at source; otherwise the excess 20% WHT can be reclaimed as a refund through ETA central office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 45 – Net tax due / refund claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after deducting quarterly advances, prior-period payments, WHT credits, and any investment tax credits under Law 72/2017; or the refund claimed per Art. 48 of the Tax Procedures Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any quarterly advance payment was underpaid, a monthly delay surcharge of 2.5% is automatically computed. Refunds to non-residents are subject to bank account verification, tax clearance certificate, and supporting TRC when DTA relief was applied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative penalty from EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 per return; late payment: a monthly surcharge of 2.5% on outstanding tax, charged per month or part of a month, without upper limit. Failure to maintain or file transfer pricing documentation: penalty up to EGP 2,000,000 plus interest. Non-filing of Form 100 for a shareholder company: criminal court may impose a fine equal to 3–5 times the tax evaded and/or imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for dividends or distributive shares distributed by an Egyptian LLC to a non-resident shareholder, unless exempted by domestic provisions (e.g., resident Egyptian corporate shareholder with long-term strategic holding) or reduced under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for treaty relief on dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain an original or e-certified Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority for the relevant fiscal year; (2) provide a Beneficial Ownership Declaration and a DTA Relief Application to the Egyptian resident payer at least 15 days before the distribution; (3) submit the package to the ETA's International Taxation Department via the e-portal for a binding reduced-withholding ruling; (4) the Egyptian payer withholds at the reduced treaty rate only after ETA approval; if tax was over-withheld, file a refund claim with the TRC, calculation schedule, and proof of remittance. For Egyptian CFC/pass-through structures, the intermediate company must demonstrate commercial substance and be the actual owner to avoid later DTA denial.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT on interest paid to non-residents for loans and on royalties/licence fees for patents, trademarks, software, and know-how is 20%. DTA reduced rates commonly applied in Egypt–EU/other bilateral treaties: interest for financial institutions 10% and 15% for other lenders; royalties generally 5%–15% depending on asset class and recipient. Management and technical-service fees are not separately classified; they fall within the 20% domestic WHT and are often treated as commercial profits or royalties according to the substance. Contracts should expressly label fees and require a gross-up clause only if permissible under treaty; otherwise, netting provisions of Law 79/2016 may cap deduction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year; or EGP 5,000,000 for controlled services and/or intangible-related transactions; where either threshold is crossed, contemporaneous Transfer Pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) must be prepared in Arabic and English and filed together with Form 100.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute (as in offshore Caribbean jurisdictions), but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in Article 72 of Law No. 82/2016 denies tax benefits from arrangements with wholly artificial transactions lacking genuine economic purpose, personnel, premises, and local risk control. A shell Egyptian LLC used to pass EPC contracts through a low-tax affiliate without Egyptian office, staff, equipment, or procurement function will be disregarded for tax purposes; the ETA may re-characterize the income as the parent's business profit and levy 22.5% corporate tax plus 2.5% monthly delay surcharges. For DSAR / CRS transparency, the LLC's economic substance declaration is a condition for obtaining a resident-trust/corporate certificate and for applying DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion / False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing invoices without real mechanical EPC service or for fabricated sub-contract work; using reverse-charge invoices to overstate costs; under-declaring milestone revenue from a hyperscale datacenter construction contract; manipulating contract price through side letters, or failing to account for Foreign Exchange (FX) gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment for 3–5 years and a fine equal to 2 to 5 times the tax evaded (Art. 133, Tax Procedures Law 82/2016). In addition, the ETA applies a 2.5% monthly late-payment surcharge and interest, and may impose a civil penalty up to EGP 2 million for TP documentation infractions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations, approve fabricated invoices, or fail to exercise supervisory functions are held jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, in addition to penal sanctions; Egyptian courts may issue a travel ban and an asset freeze against directors, and a block of repatriation of funds until a final tax clearance is issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Activity / Artificial Economic Substance Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Constituting the Egyptian LLC as a pure pass-through, with no physical office in Egypt, no substantive operational officers, no local decision-making, no ultimate risk of the EPC contract, and a board that never meets; routing contracts through a Cyprus or UAE mailbox only to claim treaty withholding benefits on margin as a 'technical service provider'.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The GAAR applies to re-characterize the LLC as a sham: corporate tax is recalculated on the full Egyptian-source profit at 22.5% plus late-payment monthly surcharges and a penalty of 3% of the assessed tax. The Ministry of Finance may also void the DTA residency certificate; criminal prosecution for tax evasion could follow if false declarations were used.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the foreign parent and of the Egyptian LLC who caused the shell structure may be jointly liable for the restated tax; travel bans and entry bans to Egypt are available for foreign directors under the ETA's collection measures. For AML/CFT, a shell structure is also a red flag that may expose directors to asset confiscation proceedings under Law 78/2016 on Anti-Money Laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Undocumented Controlled Transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging above-market fees for related engineering design or cooling-system software licensing; paying inflated intercompany management fees to a related company in a zero-tax jurisdiction; failing to prepare and maintain Local File and Master File where related party EPC subcontracting, financing, or intellectual property flows exceed the EGP 10 million threshold; applying an unjustified gross margin to the EPC contractor's sub-contractor chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA reassessment at arm's length methods (CUP, RPM, CPLM, TNMM, PSM) plus a monthly 2.5% delay surcharge; separate penalty up to EGP 2,000,000 for incomplete or non-contemporaneous TP documentation; a further 2% penalty for erroneous tax return accuracy. If the mis-pricing is held to be intentional evasion, the criminal penalties under Law 82/2016 apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the intercompany pricing or failed to ensure documentation requirements may be personally liable for the additional corporate tax, and may be charged with tax evasion if the TP manipulation was intentional and concealed; professional indemnity claims and disqualification from holding EPC public-sector contracts can also arise.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Terrorist Financing Exposure in EPC Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving large milestone payments from state-owned or sovereign-linked counterparties without conducting simplified due diligence; accepting milestone payments routed through third-party intermediary bank accounts with no ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration; using cash-heavy subcontractor payments for labor-intensive cooling tower repairs that mimic legitimate EPC flow but disguise kickbacks to public officials; failing to report suspicious transactions under Law 80/2002 and its 2016 amendments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Anti-Money Laundering Law (Law No. 93/2018) imposes imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a fine of EGP 200,000 to EGP 1,000,000; the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFIU) can issue freezing orders without judicial review. The ETA may also treat laundered funds as deemed income and levy 22.5% tax plus surcharges; the contract with a government-related entity is automatically suspended on a red flag.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal prosecution for failure to establish AML compliance functions if the LLC is caught accepting unexplained third-party payments or laundering proceeds in construction contracts; travel bans, travel restrictions, and freezing of personal assets are routinely ordered. Under the Egyptian Criminal Code, directors who knowingly or negligently fail to prevent the money-laundering activity are liable as principals.
